en.heading: April: Filipino food as living cultural heritage
en.origin: Filipino Food Month celebrates dishes, preparation techniques and food traditions as expressions of Philippine cultural heritage, not only as products of the restaurant industry. Proclamation No. 469, signed in April 2018, established April of every year as Buwan ng Kalutong Pilipino; it expressly links culinary traditions to the 2009 National Cultural Heritage Act's implementing rules. The proclamation assigns leadership to the Department of Agriculture and NCCA and invites government, schools and local communities to take part; it explicitly recognizes farmers and agricultural livelihoods.
en.promoter: Department of Agriculture and National Commission for Culture and the Arts were designated or identified as coordinating public institutions for this Philippine observance.
en.purpose: Preserve food knowledge across generations while recognizing the communities and farmers behind traditional Philippine cuisine.

en.heading: April: Philippine literature across many languages
en.origin: National Literature Month, also called Buwan ng Panitikang Filipino, highlights writing and storytelling in the Philippines' different languages and the ways books carry history and collective memory. President Benigno Aquino III issued Proclamation No. 968 on 10 February 2015 to designate April; the text mentions the April remembrance of poet Francisco Balagtas and other literary anniversaries. The NCCA and the Commission on the Filipino Language were designated as coordinating institutions; this national month is distinct from individual authors' birthdays and from UNESCO's World Book Day.
en.promoter: National Commission for Culture and the Arts and Komisyon sa Wikang Filipino were designated or identified as coordinating public institutions for this Philippine observance.
en.purpose: Promote Philippine literary heritage and contemporary reading and writing in the country's many languages.

en.heading: August: a History Month that replaced a September week
en.origin: Philippine History Month invites schools, museums and communities to examine the country's turning points, local memories and historical interpretation over an entire month. Proclamation No. 339, signed on 16 February 2012, moved the older History Week of 15–21 September, created under Proclamation No. 1304 of 1974, to the whole of August and repealed that 1974 order. The decree cited the concentration of important August events and argued a single week was insufficient; it must not be mistaken for the legal establishment of National Heroes Day itself.
en.promoter: National Historical Commission of the Philippines and cultural education institutions were designated or identified as coordinating public institutions for this Philippine observance.
en.purpose: Encourage accurate public history, local heritage research and awareness of national historical turning points.

Il decreto richiamava i numerosi avvenimenti di agosto e la necessità di più tempo rispetto a una settimana; non istituisce la distinta Giornata degli eroi nazionali.

en.heading: October: Museums and Galleries Month preserves cultural memory
en.origin: Museums and Galleries Month offers a national occasion to explore collections, archives, art, historic objects and the many cultural traditions that shape Philippine identity. President Corazon Aquino signed Proclamation No. 798 on 12 September 1991, establishing October annually and linking the initiative to cultural preservation and the World Decade for Cultural Development. The then Presidential Commission on Culture and Arts was designated to lead activities, with museums and galleries urged to participate; the proclamation precedes the later institutional framework of today's NCCA.

en.purpose: Broaden access to collections and cultural learning and support preservation of Philippine heritage.

en.heading: November: Children's Month moved from October by a 2015 law
en.origin: National Children's Month supports the rights and wellbeing of Filipino children and brings public attention to the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, adopted on 20 November 1989. A 1993 proclamation had declared October National Children's Month. Republic Act No. 10661, approved on 29 May 2015, explicitly changed the recurring month to November and repealed the earlier proclamations. The law names social-welfare, youth and children's councils as leading agencies; the current November calendar must not be shown as if the October designation had never existed.
en.promoter: Department of Social Welfare and Development, National Youth Commission and Council for the Welfare of Children were designated or identified as coordinating public institutions for this Philippine observance.
en.purpose: Strengthen children's rights and public understanding of the UN Convention through schools and communities.

it.heading: Novembre: una legge del 2015 ha spostato il Mese dei bambini
it.origin: Il Mese dei bambini promuove diritti e benessere dell'infanzia filippina, richiamando la Convenzione ONU sui diritti del fanciullo adottata il 20 novembre 1989. Una proclamazione del 1993 prevedeva ottobre. La Legge della Repubblica n. 10661, approvata il 29 maggio 2015, fissò novembre e abrogò espressamente le proclamazioni precedenti. La legge affida il coordinamento agli enti per benessere sociale, giovani e infanzia; il calendario di novembre non deve cancellare la precedente origine di ottobre.

de.heading: November: Ein Gesetz von 2015 verlegte den Kindermonat
de.origin: Der nationale Kindermonat stärkt Kinderrechte in den Philippinen und erinnert an die UN-Kinderrechtskonvention vom 20. November 1989. Eine Proklamation von 1993 hatte Oktober vorgesehen. Republikgesetz Nr. 10661 vom 29. Mai 2015 verlegte den Monat ausdrücklich auf November und hob die früheren Verordnungen auf. Das Gesetz beauftragt Sozial-, Jugend- und Kinderschutzstellen; die heutige Novemberregel darf die frühere Oktoberregelung nicht ausblenden.

en.heading: October: Indigenous Peoples Month has a separate 2009 origin
en.origin: National Indigenous Peoples Month celebrates the diverse cultures of Philippine indigenous peoples and calls for protection of their rights, traditions and participation in public life. Proclamation No. 1906 of 5 October 2009 established the whole month of October, building on the 1997 Indigenous Peoples Rights Act and an October 29 Thanksgiving Day previously recognized in 2003. The NCCA's Subcommission on Cultural Communities and Traditional Arts was assigned a leading role; month-long celebration and single-day Thanksgiving remain different legal observances.
en.promoter: National Commission for Culture and the Arts and National Commission on Indigenous Peoples were designated or identified as coordinating public institutions for this Philippine observance.
en.purpose: Support indigenous cultural rights, community heritage and respectful public participation.

it.heading: Ottobre: il Mese dei popoli indigeni ha una propria origine nel 2009
it.origin: Il Mese dei popoli indigeni riconosce la pluralità delle culture indigene filippine e richiama la tutela di diritti, tradizioni e partecipazione alla vita pubblica. La Proclamazione n. 1906 del 5 ottobre 2009 istituì l'intero ottobre, richiamando la legge sui diritti indigeni del 1997 e la distinta giornata di ringraziamento del 29 ottobre, riconosciuta nel 2003. La sottocommissione NCCA per comunità culturali e arti tradizionali ricevette un ruolo guida; il mese intero e la giornata del 29 ottobre restano ricorrenze giuridiche distinte.
